judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: This is a home-page story card: <a href> wrapping <article><header><label class=kicker> + <h3>, with text 'JUSTIÇA DO TRABALHO Contratada como balconista, funcionária é deslocada para a cozinha, s…'. Chrome's CDP tree really does give this link an empty name, as it does all 65 article-wrapping card links on the page, because Chrome does not let <article> content count towards name-from-content. Against the finding: AccName 1.2 step 2H includes the article's descendants, so the spec-computed name (and axe's, and the ACT link-name rule's) is the visible headline. NVDA and JAWS read the link's content, and the h3 inside it is reachable by heading navigation. For the finding: some pairings (Narrator, or TalkBack with Chrome, per testing of the analogous figure-in-link pattern) announce only 'link' or the URL. So this is Chrome's exposure deviating from spec-conformant markup, and competent auditors would split on calling it a 4.1.2 failure. The live page still uses the same markup.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: h1 'Entretenimento' heads a home-page section whose 'veja mais' link goes to /entretenimento. The heading describes the section's topic, so 2.4.6 is met and the claim that it names a different topic does not hold.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: 'Top Gadget Insider' is the advertiser line of a Taboola sponsored card, rendered in the main document (#internal_trc_…), not in an iframe. I sampled the screenshot: the text is #1084c0 on #f4f7f8, which gives 3.84:1, at 11px bold, so it is not large text. The logotype exception does not cover it, because the 1.4.3 Understanding text exempts logos and logotypes and says brand-driven plain text is not exempt. Third-party content still counts towards the page's conformance. It fails 4.5:1.

Against the finding: AccName 1.2 step 2H includes the article's descendants, so the spec-computed name (and axe's, and the ACT link-name rule's) is the visible headline. NVDA and JAWS read the link's content, and the h3 inside it is reachable by heading navigation. For the finding: some pairings (Narrator, or TalkBack with Chrome, per testing of the analogous figure-in-link pattern) announce only 'link' or the URL. So this is Chrome's exposure deviating from spec-conformant markup, and competent auditors would split on calling it a 4.1.2 failure. The live page still uses the same markup.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: 'Fuugu' is the advertiser line of a Taboola sponsored card in the main document. I sampled the screenshot: the text is #1084c0 on #f4f7f8, which gives 3.84:1, at 11px bold, so it is not large text. Plain-text brand names are not covered by the logotype exception (1.4.3 Understanding), and third-party content still counts. It fails 4.5:1.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the footer 'Versão Impressa' block (div.versao-digital-container). The live HTML shows onclick="openNewWindow('https://impresso.correio24horas.com.br/…')" and cursor:pointer on it. It has no role and no tabindex, and there is no link or button inside it, only an img (alt 'Miniatura Jornal') and text. The snapshot's CDP tree exposes it as generic with a click listener. A script-driven control on a div with no role is documented failure F59 of 4.1.2, and it is also not keyboard operable. No technique makes it pass.
